what_was_done: T-HISTORY now defines sync.remote_head as the last head of the remote whose arrivals this clone checked and took into its mount, and says that the check itself reads it and never writes it. It is written in two places, each only after the mount holds the commit: by step 4 of the sync, once what arrived is checked and the mount is fast-forwarded, to the fetched head; and when a push of this clone is accepted, to the pushed commit and not to the remote's head. A fetch made to judge a push writes nothing in the mount or the clone record (T-PUSH says so where it makes that fetch), so after a lost race the field is still the push's base, and the repeated sync, and T-PUBLISH's and T-MINT's repeated opening sync, list what arrived from that base through T-INCOMING, whose `reads` now names the field. command:sync follows: step 3 ends `synced` without a fetch only when the listed head is sync.remote_head, the mount's head is that commit too, sync.unknown is empty and, in a full sync, the clone holds no claim that T-RELEASE has a sync remove; step 4 writes the clone record after the fast-forward and not before; step 5 returns to step 3 with the field as it was. The last two conditions of step 3 go past the proposal, because the shortcut also skipped step 4's own work: on a quiet remote a commit in sync.unknown was never settled, so a minting command stayed refused. record:clone, schema:clone, T-REMOTE's wording and the reason in topic:team-sync say the same by reference. Run on git 2.34.1 and 2.50.1 in scratch repositories, three rounds each (team-git-facts, fact 20): after a lost race, diff-tree from the push's base to the new head lists a record made by hand and the winner's claim, the same listing from the judged head to itself is empty, and the fast-forward of the mount to the accepted claim commit alone put that record into the mount; after a push that was taken while its answer was lost and a commit pushed on top, merge --ff-only of the pushed commit moves the mount to that commit and not to the remote's head, and the listing from the pushed commit names the later file. The full sync, the claim taken by two clones at once and the hand-off were walked again with this rule (fact 18). Proof scenario 2 gains both cases, with the broken record reported through T-INCOMING. Ledger D33-3 is reworded.

The last section of topics/team-sync.md keeps no list of its own: it says that which of the checks the file explains act while team.enabled is false is stated once, at the head of table:team-checks, and keeps the sentence "With no remote there is nothing to sync and nothing changes." A search of every D33 file for the same statement found it in two more places, both corrected. command:sync said that with team use off the command does the state push "and nothing else, with T-SOLO"; it now points to the head rule for the checks that act on that push. T-SOLO said it "is the only thing that changes for a project with one clone", which the head rule contradicts (T-REMOTE's remote and refs, T-JOIN, T-ORDER, the hand-commit checks and T-DELIVERY in pr mode act too); it now says only that with no second clone the remote never moves and T-SOLO never runs. Ledger D33-3 said "nothing changes but T-SOLO" and is reworded. The statements left in topic:state-commits, topic:run-lock and record:lock describe T-SOLO alone and claim no list.

T-MINT no longer keys on the kind of id. When a minting push ends `unknown`, the clone record lists the commit with its request: the SHA-256 of the kind of id and of every value the caller gave for the new file, and of nothing the tool adds (the id, a time, the run, the clone, the person). The entries of sync.unknown are now objects {commit, request}, the sync copies the request into the `settled` entry, and the digest is defined once, in record:clone, and computed by one function of package M3 for every minting command, with a test that the same request has the same digest under any id and on any day and that another title or text has another. After its opening sync, which settles every unknown commit, a minting command looks in `settled` for its own request. An entry the remote took is the lost answer: the command returns that id, removes the entry and mints nothing. An entry the remote did not take is removed and the command mints. A command with any other request mints as usual and leaves the entries, so a second idea or change request is never answered with the first one's id. The stored digest was chosen over comparing the file the command would write with the minted one, because it is one function for six commands and needs no list, per kind of file, of the fields to leave out. T-MINT's `unmeasured` cell states what remains: a request worded differently after a lost answer is minted again, and the settled entry stays listed for a person. schema:clone, T-PUSH's `unknown` case, ledger D33-16 and the deliverables of M3 follow. Proof scenario 30 gains a different change request filed after the settled lost answer: it gets a new id and a new file, and vsdd status still lists the entry. No git command is concerned.

T-BRANCH's `runs` cell is now the one statement of when the remote is asked about a story branch: only where the story's closure records delivery.pushed or the local branch has an upstream, both read without the network (tracked state, and %(upstream:remotename) of git for-each-ref). Such a branch is looked for on the remote and fetched where it is there; where it is not, nothing arrived. A branch with neither has no push on record and the remote is not asked about it, so a project in local mode makes no network call, and its first push is judged by a fetch as every push is, which finds whatever is there. The head rule of table:team-checks no longer says "wherever the branch they read has an upstream" and refers to each row's `runs` cell; topic:team-delivery and the D33 passages of command:survey and command:story-deliver link to the cell and restate no condition. Two things the git runs showed are corrected with it (2.34.1 and 2.50.1, three rounds each; team-git-facts, facts 19 and 21). git ls-remote matches a pattern at the end of a name: with only keep/refs/heads/story/S-6 on the remote, a listing of refs/heads/story/S-6 exits 0, so the exit status alone does not say that the branch is there. A new head rule has every listing read by the exact ref name, through one function of package M1, and T-HISTORY reads through it as T-BRANCH does. And the upstream stays recorded after the branch is deleted on the remote, where the listing exits 2 and a fetch 128: T-BRANCH gains a fifth blocked case, the branch gone while this clone does not hold the commit delivery.pushed names. Proof scenario 23 asserts no listing of the remote in local mode, and scenario 38 that no listing names a story branch before its first push. Ledger D33-17 follows. One gap seen here and not closed is recorded as the new entry D33-34 for package M4: the listings and fetches the survey makes for held stories have each a time limit but no shared budget, and no row says what the survey does with a story whose branch could not be read.
